name: silt_loam_loess

source.theta_fc: [C] inside the FAO-56 Table 19 silt loam range 0.22-0.36 (Allen et al. 1998, ch. 7); the value is [AS], a loess-derived arable soil of the Rhein-Main lowlands.
source.theta_wp: [C] inside the FAO-56 Table 19 silt loam range 0.09-0.21; the value is [AS]. theta_fc - theta_wp = 0.17 m3/m3 is inside the Table 19 range 0.13-0.19.
source.depth_m: [AS] depth of the water bucket (deep loess, rooting is limited by the crop, not the soil, down to 1.8 m).
source.fallow_root_depth_m: [AS] depth of the 'root zone' bucket of bare soil: the layer that exchanges water with the surface within days.

source.depth_m: [C] Ze = 0.10-0.15 m (FAO-56 ch. 7, Table 19 is tabulated for Ze = 0.10 m).
source.rew_mm: [C] FAO-56 Table 19, silt loam REW 8-11 mm; midpoint. TEW is derived (eq 73) = 1000 (theta_fc - 0.5 theta_wp) Ze = 23.5 mm, inside the Table 19 range 18-25.

source.curve_number_ii: [AS] SCS curve number for average antecedent moisture, small grain, straight row, good condition, hydrologic soil group B (USDA NRCS NEH-4 table, recalled from memory, not re-read).
source.cn_normal_wetness: [AS] relative root-zone wetness (1 = field capacity) at which CN_II applies; CN_I and CN_III are interpolated below and above it with the standard conversion formulas.
source.ia_ratio: [C] initial abstraction 0.2 S, the classical NEH-4 ratio.

source.melt_mm_per_k_day: [AS] degree-day factor of the snow store, typical lowland range 2-4 mm per K per day.

source.min_q10: [AS] Q10 of the biological rates; the usual textbook value 2, recalled, not verified in a document.
source.min_moisture_floor: [AS] moisture factor of a dry root zone; rises linearly to 1 at field capacity.
source.fresh_rate_per_day_20c: [AS] first-order mineralisation of the fresh organic N pool (manure, residues) at 20 degC and field capacity.
source.nitrif_rate_per_day_20c: [AS] first-order nitrification of ammonium at 20 degC and field capacity (half-life about a week).
source.denit_rate_per_day_20c: [AS] first-order nitrate loss of the root layer at 20 degC when wet.
source.denit_wetness: [AS] relative root-zone wetness above which denitrification runs, linear to 1 at field capacity.
source.soil_t_lag_days: [AS] soil temperature follows the daily mean air temperature with this time constant.
source.soil_t_ramp_c: [AS] biological rates ramp from 0 at 0 degC to the Q10 law at this soil temperature.
source.n_deposition_kg_ha_day: [AS] 20 kg N/ha/yr (/365) booked as ammonium: the lower end of the 20-70 kg N/ha/yr German load range (UBA 1995 as quoted by UFZ, search snippet only).
source.nh3_temp_q10: [AS] rate factor per 10 K of the surface volatilisation around 15 degC; reproduces cold-March < 35 % and warm-June about 60 % of the NH4 lost for cattle slurry (LfL Versuchsbericht 2017).
source.soil_test_kg_per_mg100g: [D] plough layer 0.3 m x bulk density 1.4 t/m3 = 4200 t/ha; 1 mg/100 g = 10 g/t, so 42 kg/ha per mg/100 g.
source.lime_react_per_day: [AS] reaction rate of incorporated lime (half-life about 90 days); no cited value found.
source.lime_surface_factor: [AS] relative reaction rate of lime left on the surface.
source.ph_avail_full: [AS] pH (CaCl2) at and above which mineralisation and P/K availability are unrestricted.
source.ph_avail_floor: [AS] pH at and below which they are at avail_floor_factor.
source.no3_init_kg_ha: [AS] spring Nmin of an arable field, typical 30-60 kg N/ha.
source.org_n_kg_ha: [AS] 0.15 % Nt (recalled range 0.12-0.18 %) x 3900 t/ha (0.3 m x 1.3 t/m3).
source.min_rate_per_day_20c: [AS] set so the net mineralisation is about 80 kg N/ha/yr (recalled 60-100 kg N/ha/yr on loess arable soil); see the measured value in the nutrient tests.
source.p_test_init_mg100g: [AS] inside VDLUFA class C 8-18 mg P2O5/100 g (Hessisches Landeslabor, Erlaeuterungen Bodenuntersuchung Acker und Gruenland (2024), Tab. 1-5 Tab. 5a).
source.p_eq_mg100g: [AS] test value the reserve replenishes to and available P above it fixes down to.
source.p_release_per_day: [AS] fraction of the gap to equilibrium released per day.
source.p_fix_per_day: [AS] fraction of the excess above equilibrium fixed per day.
source.p_rel_b: [AS] Mitscherlich coefficient per mg/100 g; no relative-yield-per-class statement was found.
source.p_target_mg100g: [C] lower bound of VDLUFA class C for P (CAL), Hessisches Landeslabor, Erlaeuterungen Bodenuntersuchung Acker und Gruenland (2024), Tab. 1-5 Tab. 5a.
source.k_test_init_mg100g: [AS] inside VDLUFA class C 12-20 mg K2O/100 g for BAG II (Hessisches Landeslabor, Erlaeuterungen Bodenuntersuchung Acker und Gruenland (2024), Tab. 1-5 Tab. 5b).
source.k_target_mg100g: [C] lower bound of VDLUFA class C for K, BAG II (Hessisches Landeslabor, Erlaeuterungen Bodenuntersuchung Acker und Gruenland (2024), Tab. 1-5 Tab. 5b).
source.ph_init: [AS] pH (CaCl2); inside the BAG II class C target 5.2-6.1 (Hessisches Landeslabor, Erlaeuterungen Bodenuntersuchung Acker und Gruenland (2024), Tab. 1-5 Tab. 2a).
source.buffer_cao_kg_ha_per_ph: [D] mean slope of the lime requirement of silty loam to loamy sand (BAG 3-5), 117 / 75 / 50 / 25 dt CaO/ha at pH 4.0 / 5.0 / 5.5 / 6.0: (117 - 25) / 2 = 46 dt CaO per pH unit (LfL Bayern, Basisdaten Duengung und Naehrstoffflusse Bas22 (12/2021) Tab. 8a).
source.cao_loss_kg_ha_per_mm_drain: [AS] base loss per mm of water leaving the root zone; set so the unavoidable annual loss of the farm climate lies inside the cited 200-570 kg CaO/ha (DLG-Merkblatt 456, Hinweise zur Kalkung (2022) Tab. 1: 300-600 for medium soils, 600-750 mm); fertiliser acidity is booked separately from the neutralising value of the material.

source.layer_a_m: [AS] thickness of the upper layer of the management model (the seedbed and the layer a cultivator mixes).
source.layer_b_m: [AS] thickness of the lower layer; the two together are the 0.30 m plough layer of the nutrient model.
source.workable_wet_full: [AS] relative root-zone wetness (0 wilting point, 1 field capacity) up to which tillage works fully; the workable window of a loam is wet-limited a little below field capacity (recalled, no document).
source.workable_wet_zero: [AS] wetness at which tillage works not at all (smearing, clods).
source.workable_dry_zero: [AS] wetness below which the soil is too hard to work (clods).
source.workable_dry_full: [AS] wetness above which a dry-side limit no longer applies.
source.damage_gain: [AS] structure damage (compaction/smearing) added by a full-depth pass in soil at zero workability; a silt loam smears more than a sandy loam.
source.damage_recovery_per_day: [AS] recovery of structure damage by frost and biology, about 1 - exp(-0.25) per year.
source.damage_cn_increase: [AS] SCS curve number added at damage 1 (surface sealing, slower infiltration).
source.damage_root_penalty: [AS] share of the maximum rooting depth lost at damage 1.
source.loose_cn_decrease: [AS] SCS curve number removed at loosening 1 (rough surface holds rain; the NRCS curve-number tables give about 4-6 units between a smooth and a rough fallow, recalled).
source.loose_stage2_evap_reduction: [AS] share of stage-2 soil evaporation removed at loosening 1 (a dry loose layer is a mulch).
source.settle_per_mm_rain: [AS] share of the loosening lost per mm of rain (about 20 mm halves it).
source.settle_per_day: [AS] share of the loosening lost per day.
source.tillage_dry_out_mm_per_m: [AS] water lost the day a moist soil is opened, per m of working depth (about 4-5 mm for a 25 cm ploughing).
source.seedbed_rest: [AS] seedbed quality of consolidated untilled soil (0 clods .. 1 fine).
source.seedbed_wet_floor: [AS] seedbed quality a tool leaves at zero workability.
source.seedbed_settle_per_mm: [AS] approach of the seedbed to its rest value per mm of rain (slaking, crusting).
source.cover_per_t_ha: [AS] soil cover by residue = 1 - exp(-A m), m in t/ha dry matter; Gregory (1982) gives the form, A about 0.2-0.4 per t/ha for small-grain straw is recalled from the NRCS residue-cover tables, not checked in a document.
source.mulch_evap_max_reduction: [C] FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998) ch. 11: organic mulch reduces soil evaporation by about 5 % for each 10 % of the soil covered, i.e. 50 % at full cover.
source.res_c_fraction: [C] carbon share of plant dry matter, about 0.44 (0.40-0.48 in the straw literature).
source.res_k20_per_day: [AS] first-order decomposition of buried straw at 20 degC and optimum moisture; with the Q10 and moisture factors the loss of buried wheat straw is about 60-70 % in the first year (recalled range from litterbag studies).
source.res_surface_factor: [AS] loose straw lying on the surface decomposes at this share of the buried rate (drier, less soil contact).
source.res_stubble_factor: [AS] standing stubble decomposes at this share of the buried rate.
source.res_moisture_floor: [AS] moisture factor of dry residue; rises linearly to 1 with the wetness of its layer.
source.res_chop_gain: [AS] decomposition of fully chopped straw is faster by this share (more surface, better contact).
source.res_assim_eff: [AS] share of decomposed carbon built into microbial biomass and kept as humus (carbon use efficiency of soil microbes about 0.3-0.5, recalled).
source.res_cn_bio: [AS] C:N of the microbial biomass, about 8-9 (Cleveland and Liptzin 2007, recalled).
source.res_n_floor_kg_ha: [AS] mineral N the decomposers cannot take.

source: F1a reference soil of the home region (loess silt loam); the numbers that are not [C] ranges are assumptions, see each block.

source.layer_depth_m: [AS] the plough layer; the organic N of the nutrient block (org_n_kg_ha) is the N of this layer.
source.bulk_density_t_m3: [AS] dry bulk density of a loamy arable topsoil, 1.3 t/m3; with 0.3 m it gives the 3900 t/ha of dry soil that the org_n_kg_ha note of the nutrient block uses.
source.humus_cn: [AS] C:N of soil organic matter is close to 10 in cultivated mineral topsoils (recalled, not checked against a source: textbook value; Batjes 1996 is recalled as 10-12 for 0-30 cm).
source.rate_per_day_20c: [D] first-order decay of the whole humus pool at 20 degC, optimum moisture and pH: the ICBM old-pool rate k2 = 0.00605 per year (Andren and Kaetterer 1997, Ecol. Appl. 7:1226, as shipped in the SoilR package defaults), divided by the mean of the model's temperature x moisture x pH factors on the home climate (measured on a bare fallow run of this model with ps_field_run) so that the pool decays at k2 per year in the mean. Not tuned to a yield or to a long-term experiment. Measured: a bare fallow run of 11 years on the home climate with the nutrient rate 1.15e-4 decays the humus at 0.01655 per year, so the rate is 1.15e-4 x 0.00605 / 0.01655 = 4.2e-5; the same run with 4.2e-5 gives 0.006046 per year.
source.humification: [C] ICBM humification coefficient h = 0.125: the share of the decomposed young-pool (residue) carbon that is passed to the old pool (Andren and Kaetterer 1997; SoilR examples use 0.125 for crop residues, 0.25 for manure). The carbon of a residue that is not humified is respired as the biomass turns over.
source.awc_per_soc_pct: [C] plant-available water capacity rises by 1.16 mm per 100 mm of soil per 1 % soil organic carbon, i.e. 0.0116 m3/m3 per 1 % (Minasny and McBratney 2018, 'Limited effect of organic matter on soil available water capacity', Eur. J. Soil Sci. 69:39-47); all of it is put on theta_fc.
